Remove a person from the middle of a group photo, close the gap as if they were never there, and do it all without touching Photoshop. That option is now sitting inside Lightroom for anyone who has never gotten comfortable with layers and masks.
Glyn Dewis walks through the exact workflow using a shot from his I Am Lyme project, a picture he grabbed with the Scallop Diver Dorset crew at the end of a shoot. He starts by testing the built-in remove tool in Lightroom with generative AI checked, and the result is honest: the background rebuilds fairly well, but the arm and hand of the man beside him fall apart. Dewis is upfront that this video is for people who use Lightroom and stop there, not for anyone already living in Photoshop every day. His own wife is the example he reaches for, someone with phone pictures she'd love to tidy up but no interest in learning masks to do it.
The real method routes the image out to Adobe Firefly through the Photo menu, using the "Generating Firefly" option and then "Edit Photo." That sends the picture to the Firefly website, where Dewis picks his model from a list that includes Adobe's own Firefly Image 5 alongside partner models like ChatGPT's image model and Google Gemini 3.1. His prompt spells everything out: remove the person in the blue baseball cap, move the remaining three people close together, and keep the faces, hair, clothing, and coloring identical to the original. About a minute and a half later, the three men are standing together, the background is intact, and there's no sign anyone was cut out. He then shows how to check the resolution and upscale, since the regenerated image comes back smaller than the 6,060 by 4,040 original.
Credit cost is where the tradeoffs get concrete. Switching to the ChatGPT image model at high quality jumps the cost from 20 credits to 80, a real leap that Dewis flags plainly. His framing is sensible: this is an occasional job, not a daily habit, so a single 80-credit edit won't drain your balance. He also points out the one rough edge in the round trip, that Firefly hands the finished file to your downloads folder rather than dropping it straight back into the Lightroom catalog, and he'd like Adobe to close that loop.
This fits into a wider shift in how Adobe is spreading generative editing across its apps instead of locking it behind Photoshop. Firefly now sits at the center of that push, and the model picker inside it, offering ChatGPT and Gemini alongside Adobe's own engine, points to a future where you choose the right tool for a specific edit rather than committing to one. The practical takeaway extends past removing people: a prompt that names exactly what to keep, faces, hair, clothing, coloring, gives generative models far less room to invent things you don't want. That discipline carries over to any AI edit you attempt, whether you're clearing a background, removing a distraction, or reworking a crowded holiday frame. Match the resolution question to your output too, since a regenerated file often lands smaller than your camera's native file and benefits from an upscale before you print or crop.
Dewis is careful not to oversell it. He says outright that Firefly isn't better than Photoshop, and if you're comfortable there, keep going. The point is that skipping Photoshop no longer puts this kind of edit out of reach, and the work doesn't have to be professional to be worth doing. A family photo with someone you'd rather not see, a holiday shot with a stranger drifting through the back, or a snap you simply want to like a bit more all qualify.

Робочий метод — меню Photo → Generating Firefly → Edit Photo: кадр іде на сайт Firefly, де можна обрати модель — Firefly Image 5, модель зображень ChatGPT або Google Gemini 3.1. Промпт описує, кого прибрати, як зсунути решту людей і що зберегти незмінним (обличчя, волосся, одяг, кольори). Через приблизно півтори хвилини троє людей стоять поруч без слідів монтажу.

Ціна в кредитах: перемикання на модель ChatGPT у високій якості піднімає вартість з 20 до 80 кредитів за правку. Регенерований файл повертається меншим за оригінал 6060×4040, тож потрібен апскейл, а готовий результат падає в папку завантажень, а не в каталог Lightroom.
Автор підкреслює: Firefly не кращий за Photoshop, але такі правки більше не потребують шарів і масок, що відкриває їх звичайним користувачам з телефонними знімками.
means: Adobe робить видалення й перекомпонування людей доступним прямо з Lightroom через сторонні моделі (ChatGPT, Gemini) — це територія нашого Erase та GenErase. Показові вузькі місця: втрата роздільної здатності, розрив каталогу і 80 кредитів за правку. Luminar Neo може виграти, якщо GenErase поверне результат у повній роздільній здатності в межах каталогу й з прозорими лімітами, а Luminar Mobile — дати промпт-керування Erase для сімейних фото.

Google is integrating more of its services with AI, as the company announced that its personal agent, Gemini Spark, can now manage your Google Photos library. That means you can ask Gemini Spark to execute tasks in Google Photos, like editing images, curating albums, automatically creating shared albums with your favorite shots, turning concert flyer photos into calendar appointments, running workflows, and more.
On Thursday evening, Google Photos lead Shimrit Ben-Yair shared the new capabilities in a post on X , noting that the new capabilities would roll out over the next few weeks to eligible Gemini AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the U.S. in English.
The company didn’t say if or when it would roll out more broadly to international markets.
For a while now, I’ve relied on @GeminiApp and @antigravity agents across a wide range of use cases—spanning creativity, productivity, and analysis. But I’ve always dreamed of having a power agent to help me get the most out of my 143,206 photos and videos. And that day has come!… pic.twitter.com/WbnkYpattQ
The addition is yet another example of Google attempting to find product-market fit in terms of making AI appealing to consumers — in this case, by automating tedious tasks and helping people manage what are now often sizable photo libraries.
The move comes at a time when the AI industry is reckoning with the fact that it hasn’t properly sold the promise of AI to consumers. This week, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Bloomberg that the industry has “done a terrible job” communicating the benefits of technology, which has led to backlash from communities around the world.
Announcements like this from Google are part of the problem. While they may make certain tasks easier, on their own, such features don’t seem revolutionary or even, really, necessary. (It’s not that difficult to make a photo album after all.) But the competitive nature of the AI industry is pushing companies to promote every AI-infused upgrade, no matter how small, instead of waiting until the company can tell a broader story about how AI has shaped its software for the better.
To use Gemini Spark with Google Photos, you’ll need to first connect Google Photos to Gemini, then toggle on Spark in the top corner of the Gemini app, and enter your prompt.

title: Google дав агенту Gemini Spark керування бібліотекою Google Photos

full: За повідомленням TechCrunch, керівниця Google Photos Шимріт Бен-Яїр анонсувала інтеграцію 4 вересня. Користувач підключає Google Photos до Gemini, вмикає Spark у застосунку Gemini і пише запит — агент сам виконує дії з бібліотекою: редагує зображення, добирає найкращі кадри в альбоми, автоматично створює спільні альбоми, а фото афіші може перетворити на подію в календарі.

New models sell AI, but buyers still pick battery, speed
The smartphone’s upgrade pitch may now be AI, but consumers are still starting with the processor, with 29% of buyers ranking the chip as their top consideration when choosing their next smartphone in the first quarter of 2026, up from 24% a year earlier, according to Counterpoint Research.
The finding comes as smartphone makers are packing AI into devices across price segments, from flagship phones that can translate conversations and search files using natural language to more affordable models offering AI photo editing, transcription and generative tools.
An Amazon India survey of more than 40,000 respondents conducted in July found that AI features influence the purchase decision of 82% of smartphone buyers. Contextual assistance was the most wanted AI capability, cited by 25% of respondents, followed by generative photo editing at 18% and visual search at 17%.
Yet Amazon’s data also reinforces Counterpoint’s finding that the fundamentals remain important. Performance and speed were the biggest purchase drivers at 87%, followed by battery life at 79% and camera quality at 77%. Battery, in particular, remains a weakness. It was the aspect consumers most frequently said their current smartphone needs to improve, at 22%, ahead of camera at 17% and performance at 12%.
“While AI has moved from a talking point to an expectation, customers are just as clear about the fundamentals that still matter, like performance, battery and camera. They are also willing to pay more for the device that gets it right,” said Zeba Khan, director, consumer electronics, Amazon India.
“Consumers still value the fundamentals of a fast, responsive and reliable device. With increasing tech literacy and rapid innovation, consumers are now looking for the right combination of features that best fits their usage needs,” said Arushi Chawla, consumer research lead and senior analyst at Counterpoint.
The latest launches all add AI to the traditional smartphone formula of processor, camera, battery and display. Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max launched last year elevated Apple Intelligence, launched in 2024, with Image Background, Notify Me and Call Context features, adding to live translation, writing and summarisation tools and visual intelligence. This year’s models, to be announced on September 9, are rumoured to have A20 Pro chip to optimise on-device Apple Intelligence, along with possibly the brand’s first foldable smartphone.
Samsung’s latest Galaxy Z Fold8 and higher-tier Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra integrates Galaxy AI across devices. Google’s Pixel 11 Pro, launched on August 12, offers deeper Gemini integration.
The AI push is also moving into phones outside the flagship segment. OnePlus’ N6 offers AI editing tools such as AI Eraser and AI Reflection Eraser. OPPO’s Reno16 5G brings AI into the hardware and a personal memory system integrating assistants including Gemini, Perplexity and ChatGPT. Vivo’s S2 5G has AI Creation and Transcript Assist. Xiaomi’s Redmi Note 15 series brings Google Gemini, Circle to Search and Xiaomi HyperAI.
Nothing’s Phone (4b) uses Essential Space to parse screenshots and voice notes and turn them into tasks and reminders, alongside AI Eraser, voice transcription and ChatGPT-integrated widgets.
Rather than being viewed as another standalone specification, AI is increasingly embedded across tools. “As a result, AI is evolving into a feature-level consideration that can influence consumer preference and, in some cases, trigger a purchase decision,” Chawla added.
“I think smartphone differentiation is moving away from individual specifications and towards the overall user experience. Value for money will always matter, but it is becoming harder for brands built primarily around that proposition to stand out, particularly in a market where consumers are being asked to spend more,” said Akis Evagelidis, co-founder and India president of Nothing. “When you are making a bigger purchase, you want to feel that you are getting something meaningfully better, not just a longer specification sheet. This is where we believe Nothing has a strong advantage,” he added. “Our recent Phone (4b) delivered our biggest smartphone opening to date and became Flipkart’s best-selling smartphone above Rs 30,000 on Day One,” Evagelidis said.
Apple sees AI as integral to the existing smartphone experience. Craig Federighi, Apple’s senior vice-president of software engineering, said in a blog post: “Truly helpful AI must be centered on our users’ needs, deeply integrated into the products they rely on every day, grounded in personal context, and built with privacy at every step.”
OPPO sees the shift particularly in how users interact with the phone. “While camera and design will always remain important, consumers are increasingly looking at how intelligently a smartphone can adapt to the way they work, create, travel and go about their day,” said an OPPO India spokesperson.
Samsung is taking the argument beyond the individual handset and towards the wider ecosystem. “AI is getting smarter faster, and this will continue. But to change how people live, it must answer: where, how and into whose hands does this intelligence reach? This will define AI’s next chapter,” Samsung Electronics CEO and President TM Roh wrote in a blog post.
That ecosystem is becoming increasingly relevant as smartphones face competition from devices that can perform functions once associated mainly with the phone. Smartwatches handle health tracking, earbuds handle calls and voice interactions, laptops increasingly have AI assistants and smart glasses are being developed for navigation, translation and contextual information. Even OpenAI is reportedly preparing an AI-first consumer device, developed with former Apple design chief Jony Ive’s LoveFrom studio and expected in 2027. The first device is expected to be compact and screenless, while OpenAI’s longer-term ambition is reportedly to develop hardware that could eventually replace the smartphone.
For now, the smartphone remains the central device because of its portability, connectivity, app ecosystem and ability to integrate with other devices, according to Counterpoint’s Chawla.

The TourBox Elite Plus is a creative editing console designed to empower photographers and videographers to simplify their workflows and thereby have more time and energy to focus on art. With special layouts and multi-dimensional input, the Elite Plus offers artists everything they need to access hundreds of software functions with a single hand.
With Bluetooth connection for switching between computers and tablets, haptic touch, and over 400 assignable functions per preset, the Elite Plus sets itself apart as the overall winner in our best TourBox editing consoles guide. The buttons feel premium and offer high-end performance.
The Elite Plus works with a wide range of design packages, including Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and more. It sits at the pinnacle of the four consoles that TourBox sells, with a more impressive spec than the TourBox Elite , TourBox NEO, and TourBox Lite. But, with this top spec comes a premium price that only the more serious of creatives will entertain.
The Elite Plus offers a solid build that feels weighty and premium. The see through plastic means you can see some of the hardware inside which is a nice touch for users who like to feel connected to their devices. The plastic case feels robust enough although I'm not entirely sure it would withstand being dropped from height onto a solid surface. A rubber material as found on the TourBox NEO would guarantee greater longevity and deliver a more tactile experience which would be preferable.
To get the console up and running, all you need to do is download the TourBox Console software and either connect it with a USB cable or via Bluetooth. For a more portable and versatile working experience you'll want to go for the wireless option. It is also via Bluetooth that the Elite Plus can be connected to iPads or Android tablets. The Bluetooth connection was relatively reliable although there were a couple of times when I had to restart my machine to make the connection work.
The various knobs, dials, and buttons are well engineered and offer over 150 combos with the ability to assign over 400 functions to each preset. That's customisability at its best. All controls work seamlessly and reliably to deliver an effortless workflow in the likes of Photoshop, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, and other major editing applications.
One of the features that sets the Elite Plus apart from the cheaper TourBox NEO and TourBox Lite is haptic feedback. This is delivered via a wide-band vibration motor and helps to root your editing experience. My only issue with it is that the sound it produces would be better if it was a dampened a little.
The TourBox Elite Plus retails at £297 / $297, which makes it the most expensive of all TourBox products, although it's often discounted by as much as £30 / $30. For the money, you'll benefit from a solid build quality, more buttons, dials, and scrollers than you can shake a stick at, and an elevated user experience courtesy of haptic feedback.
One of the best alternatives is the 4.5-star Logitech MX Creative Console , which costs £189.99 / $189.99. This cute and compact device features two independent consoles that allow users to switch between applications and utilise buttons, a dial and a scroller to access application shortcuts. It's simpler than the Elite Plus but also a lot more affordable.
Another alternative is the XPPen Pilot Pro . It's cheaper than both the Elite Plus and the MX Creative Console and is aimed specifically at video editors who spend their time regularly switching between tools like Razor, Ripple Edit and Selection in DaVinci Resolve and Premiere.
The Elite Plus is for photographers and videographers who are editing on a daily basis. It speeds up almost all elements of the workflow across photo-editing, retouching, colour grading, and cutting videos. With an abundance of buttons it is also possible, through the TourBox Console software to customise your setup to suit your exact way of working. I also appreciated how it automatically switched mapping profiles when I moved from one piece of software to the next.
The setup was relatively straightforward although I had to restart my machine because the TourBox Console couldn't detect the device via Bluetooth. The presence of software presets meant I could get up and running with the console in less than ten minutes after unboxing.
At the price it retails at, editors who are only using the likes of Photoshop and DaVinci Resolve on an occasional basis are unlikely to reap the workflow benefits. The use of keyboard shortcuts is likely to be sufficient if you fall into this category. Other creatives such as 3D artists are also unlikely to benefit from this type of console.

full: Elite Plus офіційно працює з Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve та іншими редакторськими пакетами, пропонуючи понад 150 комбінацій керування та автоматичне перемикання профілів мапінгу при переході між застосунками. Пристрій підключається через USB або Bluetooth (у тому числі до iPad і Android-планшетів), має тактильний відгук (haptic feedback) і, за словами оглядача, налаштовується менш ніж за десять хвилин після розпакування.

means: Luminar Neo працює як плагін усередині Lightroom Classic і Photoshop, тож частина наших користувачів вже могла б використовувати такі консолі у зв'язці з Luminar — варто перевірити, чи коректно прив'язуються ярлики Luminar (Erase, Sky AI, Mask AI тощо) до апаратних кнопок TourBox і чи варто випустити офіційний пресет-профіль для популярних консолей як маркетинговий і UX-бонус.

Apple is set to introduce iOS 27 on June 8 at its annual Worldwide Developers Conference. The upcoming update is expected to bring long-awaited changes to Siri. Reports suggest that the smarter assistant may finally arrive, powered by Google Gemini models. This marks a major step in Apple’s growing focus on artificial intelligence.
At the same time, Apple is also working on several AI-driven upgrades for its Photos app. According to a recent report from Bloomberg, the app will include a new section called Apple Intelligence Tools. This section will sit inside the editing interface and offer four key features: Extend, Enhance, Reframe, and Clean Up.
First, Extend will allow users to expand an image beyond its original frame. Users can stretch the edges with their fingers to add more content. This gives better control over how much area gets added and where it appears.
Next, Enhance will focus on improving images automatically. It will adjust colors, lighting, and overall image quality using AI. While the exact improvements remain unclear, the goal is to deliver better-looking photos with minimal effort.
Meanwhile, Reframe is built for spatial photos. This format supports 3D images designed for the Apple Vision Pro headset. With Reframe, users can shift the perspective even after capturing the image. This adds more flexibility when editing immersive photos.
In addition, Clean Up will remain part of the Photos app. It is currently the only AI-powered editing tool available. The feature lets users remove unwanted objects from images, and it is expected to stay in iOS 27.
However, development has not been smooth. Sources cited by Bloomberg say that Extend and Reframe faced issues during internal testing. In some cases, they did not perform reliably. As a result, Apple may delay these features or release limited versions.
Clean Up has also received mixed feedback. Some users reported visual artifacts after editing. Others noticed distorted images or incorrect details filling removed areas. These concerns highlight the challenges Apple still faces with AI tools.

title: Apple готує чотири AI-інструменти для фото в iOS 27: Extend, Enhance, Reframe, Clean Up
lead: За даними Bloomberg, у застосунку Photos на iOS 27 з'явиться розділ Apple Intelligence Tools усередині інтерфейсу редагування з чотирма функціями. Частина з них, за словами джерел, поки нестабільно працює у внутрішньому тестуванні.
full: Extend дозволяє розширити зображення за межі оригінальної рамки — користувач розтягує краї пальцем, щоб додати більше простору навколо кадру. Enhance автоматично покращує колір, світло та загальну якість фото засобами AI, хоча Apple поки не розкриває деталі алгоритму. Reframe створений для просторових фото у 3D-форматі під Apple Vision Pro і дозволяє змінювати ракурс уже після зйомки. Clean Up залишається в застосунку без змін — це єдиний AI-інструмент редагування, вже доступний зараз, він видаляє небажані об'єкти з фото.

За даними джерел Bloomberg, Extend і Reframe показували нестабільні результати під час внутрішнього тестування, тож Apple може відкласти їх або випустити в обмеженому вигляді. Сам Clean Up також отримує неоднозначні відгуки: користувачі повідомляють про візуальні артефакти, спотворення та некоректно відновлені деталі на місці видалених об'єктів.
means: Enhance і Extend напряму перетинаються з нашими Enhance AI та GenExpand, а Clean Up — прямий аналог Erase/GenErase. Публічне визнання Apple проблем з артефактами й нестабільною генерацією підтверджує, що якість inpainting/expand лишається складною задачею навіть для tier-1 гравця — це аргумент на користь подальших інвестицій у стабільність GenErase та GenExpand у Luminar Neo, де надійність результату є конкурентною перевагою.

Photoshop's autofocus point checker inside Camera Raw 18.6 shows you exactly which points your camera locked onto, so you can catch a blurred watch face or a hand in focus before you commit to the wrong shot. That single feature answers a question you've probably asked yourself a hundred times while culling: did the camera focus where I thought it did?
Unmesh Dinda runs through 20 recent additions to Photoshop and Camera Raw, and the autofocus overlay is just the opener. Right-click a raw file, select show autofocus points, and the exact focus points appear on the image. Zoom in and the story gets clear fast. Dinda demonstrates it on a watch, where one frame nails the face and another lands on his hand instead. The shortcut is Command Option Shift O on Mac, Control Alt Shift O on Windows, and it turns the overlay on and off instantly.
Several of the strongest updates sit in Camera Raw itself. The new glow effect lives in the effects dropdown and gives you three distinct styles: diffusion, which softens highlights; bloom, which adds light on top of highlights; and halation, which wraps a colored edge around bright areas. Dinda runs it as a smart filter so it stays editable, and he shows how the highlight slider controls whether only the brightest points glow or whether softer highlights get pulled in too. There's also a vectorscope now, borrowed from video color grading, which maps where your colors land and doubles as a skin tone checker when you turn on the skin tone indicator. Match your skin tones to that diagonal line using point color, and uneven complexions fall into place.
The Camera Raw generative expand deserves attention because it works on raw files while keeping every setting intact. Enable expand in the crop section, drag out the canvas, click generate, and the extended area carries your white balance, highlights, and shadows with no visible seam. Dinda points out that this is impossible in Photoshop proper, where expansion happens on a baked-in version of the image. The blemish removal tool in the remove section keeps real skin texture instead of smoothing everything into plastic, with separate sliders for spots and for moles or birthmarks. If you'd rather avoid AI entirely, you can switch off every generative feature under the settings cog.
The through-line worth grabbing here is that Adobe keeps moving raw-native editing forward while adding a parallel AI workspace that hides layers and channels completely. Photoshop 27.1 introduced the AI-assisted mode, with markup tools, region selection, and a tune beta that shifts a scene from day to evening. That split reflects a wider shift across the industry, where destructive one-click results and precise nondestructive control now live under one roof. The practical takeaway is to treat the two as different jobs. Reach for the AI workspace when you want a fast rendered concept, then hit pro editor to drop the full image back into Photoshop for real masking, dodging, and compositing. Understanding masks, focus, and light is what lets you decide which tool actually earns the edit, rather than accepting whatever the model hands back.
A few quieter changes save time in daily work. You can now customize the save dialog file format under Edit, dragging formats like IFF and PCX out of the list so save a copy stops burying the options you use. The metadata info panel reads camera model, settings, and content credentials, and clicking the location opens the exact spot in Google Maps. Dynamic fit resizes text to fill any shape you draw, including a path made with the pen tool, adjusting the font size as you type. Color wheels have moved into masking too, so you can grade a background in one direction and your subject in another. Two new mask sliders, feather and edge, let you contract or expand a selection and soften it, which pairs well with shallow depth-of-field shots where a hard mask edge gives you away.
Give the video above a full watch to see the remaining features Dinda demonstrates, including render to DNG and the halation glow trick stacked on top of a bloom.

title: 20 нових функцій Photoshop і Camera Raw 18.6: фокус-точки, Glow, GenExpand на RAW
lead: Fstoppers зібрав 20 нещодавніх оновлень Photoshop та Camera Raw, зокрема оверлей точок автофокусу, ефект Glow, вектороскоп, генеративне розширення на RAW і збереження текстури шкіри при видаленні дефектів.
full: Camera Raw 18.6 показує точки автофокусу з RAW-файлу (правий клік → Show autofocus points, Cmd+Opt+Shift+O), що допомагає відсіювати кадри з промахом фокуса. У блоці Effects з'явився Glow з трьома стилями — Diffusion, Bloom, Halation; додано вектороскоп з індикатором тону шкіри, а колірні кола й повзунки Feather/Edge перенесені в маски.

Generative Expand у Camera Raw працює безпосередньо з RAW і зберігає баланс білого, світла й тіні без видимого шва — у самому Photoshop розширення можливе лише на запеченому зображенні. Інструмент видалення плям (blemish removal) залишає реальну текстуру шкіри з окремими повзунками для плям і родимок. Усі генеративні функції можна вимкнути в налаштуваннях.

Photoshop 27.1 отримав AI-режим без шарів і каналів: розмітка, вибір областей і бета-функція Tune, що переводить сцену з дня у вечір. Автор радить використовувати AI-режим для швидких концептів, а «Pro editor» — для масок і композитингу.
means: Adobe закриває одразу кілька наших ніш: Glow конкурує з Magic Light AI та Atmosphere AI, blemish removal із збереженням текстури — зі Skin AI, GenExpand на RAW із збереженням проявки — з нашим GenExpand, а Tune «день → вечір» перетинається з Relight AI та Twilight Enhancer. Оверлей точок автофокусу — дешева функція для кулінгу, якої в Neo немає. Окремий AI-режим без шарів підтверджує нашу ставку на простий інтерфейс.

This week, Camera Intelligence revealed the latest generative AI features in its Caira camera: adding Nano Banana video editing to its genAI photography. It was the latest reminder that the imaging industry, like the rest of the world, is doubling down on AI in its products – including the generative kind.
No hate, no shade. But it reminded me of a conversation I had with Canon earlier this year, when I asked the Japanese leadership about the subject of AI – and they were crystal clear about what is and what is not off limits when it comes to artificial intelligence.
"AI is going to keep on playing an important role for any shooting experiences for our products," said Tetsushi Hibi, advisory director of Canon's Img Optical Business Unit 1, behind closed doors at the CP+ 2026 show in Japan.
"So this is Canon’s stance: we are going to use AI not to generate imagery, but to capture scenes as close to the reality of shooting as possible – noise reduction, color correction, distortion correction, aberration – so those are the functions we are aiming to put it onto in our products."
We've already seen this in practice, particularly with the Canon EOS R1 and R5 Mark II – both of which use Canon's neural network image processing (NnIP) for features like 400% in-camera upscaling and 2-stop noise reduction. And of course, the many algorithmic subject detection and tracking options.
It is heartening to know, however, that generative AI imaging is not on the table for Canon – particularly with the company having rolled out its Authenticity Imaging System in May, offering content compliance to help verify the authenticity of images (and, by proxy, policing image manipulation and AI embelishment).
Where Canon definitely is implementing AI, however, is in the design phase.

"We have started our attempt to use AI for design," notes Hibi, which is born out by a recent company report that AI will be used in the early prototyping phase to simulate things like drop tests and assess thermal performance.
"We have no choice but to use AI in the design department," adds Go Tokura, executive vice president and head of Canon's Imaging Group. He's also sure to point out that the fruits of the technology will still be distinctly 'Canon', rather than resulting in homogenized products that are the same as other brands.
"When it comes to design, it is said that the AI can bring up the best possible solution. And you may think, if that’s the case, every single company will come up with the same new products.
"We have our own accumulated technology – not just designing capabilities, but also production technology as well, and materials. So even if we use AI for design, AI will consider all these unique capabilities to come up with the best solution for Canon .
"So even if the solution is generated by AI, that could be a good solution that will be able to differentiate our product from the others."

title: Canon: AI у камерах — для шумозаглушення й корекції, а не генерації зображень
lead: Керівництво Canon на CP+ 2026 заявило Digital Camera World, що використовуватиме AI лише для наближення знімка до реальності — денойз, корекція кольору, дисторсії та аберацій — і не планує генеративних функцій у камерах.
full: Тецуші Хібі з Canon Image Optical Business Unit 1 окреслив позицію компанії: AI має покращувати захоплення сцени, а не створювати зображення. Це вже реалізовано у EOS R1 та R5 Mark II через нейромережеву обробку NnIP: апскейл 400% у камері, шумозаглушення на 2 стопи, AI-розпізнавання й трекінг об'єктів. У травні Canon також запустила систему Authenticity Imaging для верифікації справжності знімків.

Привід для статті — камера Caira від Camera Intelligence, яка додала генеративне відеоредагування на Nano Banana до своїх genAI-фотофункцій. Canon натомість застосовує AI у проєктуванні: симуляції дроп-тестів і теплового режиму на етапі прототипування.
means: Виробники камер переносять денойз і апскейл у сам корпус (2 стопи шуму, 400% апскейл на R1/R5 II), що поступово зменшує потребу в Noiseless AI та Upscale AI на десктопі для нових камер Canon. Водночас генеративне редагування Canon свідомо залишає софту — це простір для GenErase, GenSwap, Sky AI. Тренд на верифікацію справжності (Authenticity Imaging, Content Credentials) варто врахувати в експорті з Luminar Neo.

page.text:
Photoshop's Brightness/Contrast slider is gone, replaced by a new Light adjustment layer that pulls Camera Raw controls straight into the main editor. Exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, and blacks now live in a single panel that behaves like a nondestructive version of the Camera Raw sliders many of you already trust.
Aaron Nace of PHLEARN walks through the layer and lands on a strong recommendation: skip the old Brightness/Contrast algorithm entirely. He explains that the Light layer is the newest arrival in a growing line that already includes Grain, Clarity, Dehaze, and Color. If you preferred the old behavior, double-click the Light layer, open the small hidden menu on the right side of the Properties panel, and switch the version to "Legacy." That brings Brightness/Contrast back exactly as it was, so nobody loses the tool they built their workflow around.
Slider order carries real weight here, and Nace lays out the sequence he uses every time: exposure first, then whites and blacks, then highlights and shadows, and contrast dead last. He also stresses masking. By default, a Light layer affects the entire frame, so he starts with Select Subject on the background layer before creating the adjustment, which turns the selection into a mask automatically. From there he inverts the mask with Command or Control plus I to work the background separately, dropping exposure to push the subject forward and lifting the whites to pull detail back into the sky. He repeats the process on a second Light layer for the subject alone, keeping each adjustment isolated and fully reversible.
The glow effect is where the tutorial earns a closer look. Nace stacks a third Light layer, groups it with itself using Command or Control plus G, then adds a mask to the group and paints in a radial gradient behind the figure. That double-mask trick, one on the layer and one on the group, is the part worth watching him do slowly, because the logic behind why it works is easy to lose if you only read the steps.
This shift fits a pattern Adobe has been running for a while now. Camera Raw and Lightroom have long been the home for exposure and tone work, and Photoshop is steadily absorbing those same controls as editable layers. If you shoot in raw and process there before opening a file, the Light layer lets you keep that same mental model instead of switching tools halfway through an edit. The bigger takeaway is the masking discipline itself: isolating exposure and tone to specific regions, subject versus background, is the same principle behind classic dodge and burn, and it transfers to any adjustment layer in the panel. Learn it on Light and it pays off on Color, Curves, and everything else. One quirk to expect: when you edit a layer beneath a Light layer, Photoshop temporarily hides the Light layers above it so you can see the raw effect you're adjusting. Nace demonstrates this with Grain, and it looks like a bug until you understand Adobe built it on purpose.
He also spends time on the Color layer, which brings temperature, tint, and vibrance sliders into the same nondestructive workflow, warming the image and nudging the tint toward green to match the tones already in the scene.

title: Photoshop замінив Brightness/Contrast новим шаром Light із контролями Camera Raw
lead: У Photoshop з'явився коригувальний шар Light, який виносить Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites і Blacks з Camera Raw у головний редактор як недеструктивний шар; старий алгоритм доступний у режимі Legacy.
full: Аарон Нейс (PHLEARN) пояснює, що Light — новий шар у лінійці Grain, Clarity, Dehaze і Color, які Adobe поступово переносить із Camera Raw у Photoshop. Повернути стару поведінку можна через приховане меню у панелі Properties, перемкнувши версію на Legacy.

Рекомендований порядок повзунків: Exposure, потім Whites і Blacks, далі Highlights і Shadows, Contrast — останнім. Автор радить починати з Select Subject, щоб шар автоматично отримав маску, і працювати окремими шарами Light для фону та об'єкта. Шар Color додає температуру, відтінок і vibrance у тому ж недеструктивному потоці.
Особливість поведінки: під час редагування шару під Light Photoshop тимчасово ховає шари Light вище, щоб показати чистий ефект — це зроблено навмисно.
means: Adobe зближує Photoshop і Lightroom/ACR, зменшуючи причину тримати другий редактор для тонової корекції. Для Luminar Neo це аргумент за те, щоб наші Layers працювали з тими ж RAW-контролями і автомасками Mask AI (людина, небо, фон) без додаткових кроків — сценарій «окремий шар на об'єкт і фон» уже є нашою сильною стороною. Для Mobile важливо, що навіть у Photoshop базовий потік стає «Select Subject + кілька повзунків».

page.text:
Fashion is a brutal test for AI imagery because audiences notice details. Hands, fabric, accessories, logos, styling and body proportions all have to survive close inspection. At the same time, fashion is one of the most exciting places to use generative tools because campaigns depend so heavily on visual worlds, impossible locations and fast-changing creative direction.
The best platform for a fashion team has to do more than produce an attractive portrait. It should help the team hold onto a character, preserve a product or silhouette, explore art direction and then turn the selected image into something large enough and controlled enough for real campaign use.
We ranked these tools with brand work in mind rather than generic AI art.
1. Magnific: Best overall for fashion campaign production
Magnific takes first place because fashion teams often need several kinds of AI work inside the same project. A campaign may start with mood exploration, move into model and product studies, require background or lighting changes, and end with high-resolution images plus motion assets.
Magnific’s image generator supports a broad selection of model families, including Google, Flux, GPT, Seedream, Ideogram, Recraft, Qwen, Luma and Magnific. That lets the creative team choose different strengths rather than forcing every campaign through one visual engine.
Reference-driven workflows are particularly important for fashion. A team may need to preserve a face, garment, accessory or overall styling while changing the location or composition. Different available models support references in different ways, giving the artist options when one approach is not holding the subject well enough.
The post-generation tools are equally relevant. Relighting can change the mood without rebuilding the concept. Change Camera can help explore another angle. Editing and variations speed up art-direction changes, while upscaling gives approved imagery a path toward larger delivery sizes.
Precision upscaling is a useful choice when product fidelity matters, while Creative upscaling can push texture or richness on more interpretive editorial images. Spaces also gives campaign teams a visual place to branch concepts and keep the process reusable.
2. Adobe Firefly: Best for fashion teams with professional retouchers
Fashion imagery is rarely finished at capture, whether the source is a camera or an AI model. Retouching, compositing, color work and layout are normal parts of the process. Adobe therefore has an obvious advantage.
Firefly lets generative work sit near Photoshop and other Creative Cloud tools, so an imperfect output is not a dead end. A retoucher can fix what needs fixing rather than asking the generator to reproduce the entire image because one detail is wrong.
Adobe’s multi-model direction also gives teams more generation choice while preserving that familiar finishing environment.
For established fashion houses, agencies and magazines, this may be the easiest workflow to integrate operationally. We still rank Magnific first because its AI-native model selection, upscaling and connected image-to-video workflow offer more flexibility before the final retouching stage.
3. Midjourney: Best for editorial fashion direction
Midjourney remains exceptional at fashion imagery that feels like it has an opinion. Lighting, styling, composition and atmosphere often appear more editorial than purely literal.
That makes it ideal for moodboards, pitch decks, campaign territories and experimental editorials. A creative director can explore a collection in brutalist architecture, on an unreal coastline or inside a surreal studio environment before committing to the final production route.
Midjourney is particularly good at answering “What could this campaign feel like?” It can help a team discover visual language faster than a long chain of references and written descriptions.
The trade-off is fidelity. When a specific garment, accessory or model identity must remain exact, we would move into more controlled reference and editing workflows. Midjourney is best when art direction is the hard problem.
4. Recraft: Best for fashion branding and graphic systems
Fashion campaigns are not only photographs. They also need packaging, labels, icons, invitations, graphic motifs, retail elements and digital design assets.
Recraft is strong in that world because it approaches AI from a design perspective and includes vector-oriented generation. A brand team can explore scalable graphic elements that support the campaign rather than generating another raster mood image.
This is useful for younger fashion brands that want the same visual language across social content, packaging and ecommerce. Recraft can help develop the system around the photography.
We would not rely on it alone for realistic fashion editorials, but as part of a wider campaign stack it is one of the most practical specialist tools.
5. Ideogram: Best for campaigns where typography is central
Fashion loves typography: campaign titles, magazine-style treatments, event posters, packaging and social graphics. Ideogram belongs on this list because it makes text inside generated imagery more usable than most traditional generators.
A creative team can explore the relationship between the model, product and headline during concept development instead of designing the image and typography as completely separate ideas.
That is particularly helpful in pitch work. A client can react to something that feels closer to a finished campaign composition rather than an isolated AI photo.
For final brand typography, designers should still rebuild and control the type precisely. Ideogram’s value is speed of visual thinking, not replacing a professional layout system.
6. Krea: Best for fast styling and mood experiments
Krea works well when the team wants to explore quickly. Fashion art direction often starts with small visual questions: colder light or warmer light, cleaner studio or messy backstage, glossy finish or film grain, minimal styling or something more maximal.
An interactive creative environment makes those questions easier to test. Krea encourages the team to move through possibilities rather than overthink every prompt.
We like it for pre-production and visual research, especially when a designer is trying to find the edge of a campaign before committing to a polished direction.
It ranks below the broader suites because a fashion campaign eventually needs stronger consistency, high-resolution delivery and a clearer production path.
7. ChatGPT Images: Best for creative directors who prefer giving feedback
Not every creative director wants to operate a complex generator. Many are much more comfortable describing what should change.
ChatGPT Images works well in that situation. A team can upload a reference, explain the campaign, generate a direction and keep revising in normal language. “Keep the pose, change the set.” “Make the styling sharper.” “Give us more empty space for the masthead.” Those are natural instructions in a fashion review.
The same conversation can also hold campaign context, copy ideas and creative rationale. That makes it particularly approachable for brand and marketing leaders who want to be involved in the visual process.
For controlled multi-asset production, however, we would still want a more specialized workflow around it.
8. Canva: Best for adapting approved fashion visuals into everyday content
Canva is not our first choice for generating the hero image of a luxury campaign, but it is extremely useful after that image exists.
Fashion brands need enormous amounts of adaptation: stories, feed posts, sale banners, retail screens, launch decks and regional versions. Canva lets a broader marketing team handle that production inside templates and brand controls without asking the main creative studio to resize everything.
AI generation can support those everyday needs, while the platform’s bigger value is assembly and collaboration.
For small fashion brands with limited design resources, Canva may actually be one of the most-used tools on this list even though it ranks eighth for high-end generative art direction.
Fashion AI works best when the brand stays more important than the model
The danger in fashion AI is chasing whatever aesthetic a model happens to make easily. The result may look polished but could belong to any brand. Strong creative teams work in the opposite direction: the brand defines the visual language, and the AI is selected and controlled to serve it.
Midjourney is brilliant for finding an editorial world. Adobe is the obvious finishing environment for teams with professional retouchers. Recraft and Ideogram solve important graphic-design problems around the main campaign.
Magnific wins overall because it can cover more of the journey without forcing the team into one model family. The team can explore, switch models, edit, relight, change perspective, upscale and then continue into video inside the same creative suite. That is particularly valuable when a campaign needs stills and motion that feel like part of the same system.

title: Рейтинг 8 AI-генераторів зображень для фешн-кампаній
lead: Видання iLounge протестувало вісім інструментів генерації зображень для модних рекламних кампаній і склало рейтинг за придатністю до брендової роботи: перше місце отримав Magnific, друге — Adobe Firefly, третє — Midjourney.
full: Автори оцінювали інструменти не як генератори «красивих картинок», а з погляду реальної продакшн-роботи над кампаніями: збереження персонажа чи товару, дослідження арт-напрямку і можливість довести обране зображення до якості, придатної для фінальної кампанії. Перше місце посів Magnific — за підтримку одразу кількох сімейств моделей (Google, Flux, GPT, Seedream, Ideogram, Recraft, Qwen, Luma, власна Magnific) в одному інструменті, референс-орієнтовані воркфлоу для збереження обличчя, одягу чи аксесуарів, а також постобробку: релайтинг, зміну ракурсу камери, точний (Precision) і креативний (Creative) апскейл.

Друге місце зайняв Adobe Firefly — завдяки прямій інтеграції з Photoshop та іншими інструментами Creative Cloud, що дає командам із професійними ретушерами змогу довести згенероване зображення до фінального вигляду, а не переробляти генерацію з нуля через одну деталь. Midjourney посів третє місце як інструмент для пошуку арт-напрямку та мудбордів завдяки сильному відчуттю стилю, хоча програє в точності відтворення конкретного товару чи вбрання.

Далі в рейтингу — Recraft (брендинг і графічні системи, векторна генерація), Ideogram (робота з текстом і типографікою всередині зображення), Krea (швидкі експерименти зі стилем і освітленням), ChatGPT Images (генерація через звичайні текстові інструкції для директорів, що не хочуть освоювати складний інтерфейс) і Canva, яка замикає рейтинг для генерації хіро-зображень, але лишається практичною для адаптації вже готових візуалів під соцмережі, банери й інші формати.
means: Огляд показує, що лідери ринку фешн-генерації поєднують вибір із кількох моделей із постобробкою — релайтингом і апскейлом, — тобто функціоналом, що напряму перетинається з нашими Relight AI, Supersharp AI/Upscale AI та хмарними GenErase/GenSwap/GenExpand. Варто орієнтуватися на підхід Magnific (мультимодельність plus вбудований апскейл і перехід у відео в одному середовищі) та Adobe Firefly (тісна інтеграція генерації з ретушшю в Photoshop) як бенчмарк для власного позиціонування AI-інструментів Luminar Neo серед фотографів і брендів, які працюють із кампанійним контентом.

A wildlife shot at dawn or a Milky Way frame late at night almost always comes with a tradeoff. Raise the ISO enough to get the exposure, and noise chews through the same fine detail you were trying to capture. That’s the problem ON1 spent August solving. NoNoise AI 2027 got its first public look this month, rebuilt specifically for the high-ISO situations that give generic noise reduction the most trouble. Alongside it, new training landed on relighting flat photos with Local Adjustments, a free 15-page guide for anyone just picking up a camera, and a fresh set of film-style light leaks for the Creative Library. Here’s everything new from ON1 this August.

New ON1 NoNoise AI 2027: AI Noise Reduction, TackSharp AI & Model Selector
ON1 announced NoNoise AI 2027, a rebuilt noise reduction tool aimed at the high-ISO shots that give most software the hardest time: wildlife at dawn or dusk, concerts under stage lighting, and the Milky Way at night. Remastered noise reduction models remove more noise while keeping results looking sharp and natural instead of smoothed over, whether that’s ISO 6400 for a concert or ISO 12,800 for a night sky. “It is easy to remove every trace of noise, but that often leaves a photo looking flat and over-processed, more like a painting than a photograph,” said Dan Harlacher, VP of Product at ON1. “We built NoNoise AI 2027 to preserve the small details that make an image look real.”
The release also adds a new model selector, so you can match the AI to your subject, wildlife, people, astrophotography, or scanned film, in one click, and upgrades TackSharp AI’s deblurring models to bring soft photos back into focus. NoNoise AI 2027 is open for pre-order now and ships in late September 2026.
Remastered noise reduction models built for high-ISO wildlife, concert, and night photography
New AI model selector for Wildlife, People, Astro, and scanned film
Automatic subject and background masks for applying different settings to each
Stop Losing Detail to Noise: ON1 NoNoise AI 2027, First Look
High ISO steals detail in wildlife and astro shots: feathers get soft, stars disappear. This first-look video shows NoNoise AI 2027 fixing that automatically, no sliders required, ahead of its late September release. A second short preview, published August 21, walks through the new model selector on its own, showing the Astro, Wildlife, and People models each holding onto detail a generic setting would smooth away.

Compare detail retention against a standard noise reduction pass
Preview the Astro, Wildlife, and People model selector options
A flat photo usually isn’t a lighting problem. It’s a separation problem. This tutorial shows how to build independent Subject and Background masks with Local Adjustments, then brighten the subject and deepen the background separately to create real depth in a photo that started out flat. Dynamic Contrast pulls out fine texture, and a Skylight-style Photo Filter ties the relit scene together, all non-destructively so every adjustment stays editable.

Free eBook: The Beginner’s Guide to Photography
This free 15-page guide is built for anyone picking up a camera or phone for the first time. It covers reading light, composition basics like the rule of thirds, leading lines, and framing, and how to think about focus and story before you shoot. It closes with an eight-point checklist to run through before every shot, no settings rabbit hole, no jargon, about 30 minutes to a sharper eye.
Download includes: a 15-page PDF guide covering light, composition, and focus fundamentals, plus a pre-shot checklist.
New in the Creative Library: Analog Glow Light Leaks
This new collection from Dylan Kotecki adds warm, sun-faded glow and film-style flares to a photo in seconds. It includes ten light leaks, ranging from warm amber streaks to cool blue and violet flares, for photographers who want the unpredictable character of real analog film without shooting film.
Ten light leak overlays, from warm amber to cool blue and violet tones
Ready to apply in ON1 Photo RAW’s Effects module
Get more from every photo with ON1 Photo RAW. Try it free for 30 days. No subscription required.
ON1 vs. Topaz: Which AI Photo Editing Tools Are Right for You?
ON1 Photo RAW and Topaz Labs solve different problems. ON1 is a full RAW editor, with organizing, masking, layers, and effects built into one app you buy once. Topaz sells separate, narrower AI tools built for one job each, like Topaz Photo for noise and sharpening or Topaz Gigapixel for upscaling, and as of August 2026 every Topaz tier is subscription-only. This article breaks down where each one fits, feature by feature and dollar for dollar: a single program that edits a photo start to finish favors ON1, while best-in-class upscaling or noise removal layered on top of an editor you already use is where Topaz’s specialized tools still lead.
Just Try It: A Marfa, Texas Photo Project
ON1’s Dan Harlacher spent a day in Marfa, Texas, a small art town in the middle of the West Texas desert, and turned ordinary travel shots into a pop-art series with a two-step edit in ON1 Photo RAW: Super Select AI to isolate one key element and push Dynamic Contrast on it, then an inverted mask with a Channel Mixer filter over the rest of the frame for the blown-out pinks and teal skies that give the series its false-color look. It’s a reminder that a personal project doesn’t need a plan, just a willingness to try an idea and see where it leads.
America’s 250th Anniversary Photo Contest: Meet the Winners
Entries for ON1’s America’s 250th Anniversary Photo Contest closed this summer, and the winners are in. Jeremy Pratt took the $500 grand prize for “Carved in Light,” a night shot of Mount Rushmore’s Avenue of Flags edited with Brilliance AI. Herbert Achatz placed second with a grizzly mid-catch at Katmai National Park’s Brooks Falls, and John Woodring took third with a Pikes Peak sunrise, out of hundreds of entries from photographers across the country.

Nvidia just spent $12.93 billion on a company that doesn’t make chips or models, it makes the place where 18 million developers go to find them. Hugging Face functions as something like GitHub for AI, and Nvidia isn’t buying the models sitting on it, it’s buying the distribution layer connecting those models to the hardware running them. We walk through why Nvidia explicitly promised not to require its own hardware, what that promise actually protects, and what this means for AMD and Intel.
Nvidia confirmed a $12.93 billion acquisition of Hugging Face on Thursday, sending Nvidia shares up roughly 2%. Hugging Face hosts more than 3 million models, 500,000 datasets, and 1 million applications, drawing more than 18 million developers, researchers, and creators, with more than 200,000 companies using the platform to discover, evaluate, customize, and deploy AI. The deal will close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approval.
Nvidia isn’t buying a model company here. It’s buying the distribution layer for open AI. Hugging Face has become something close to GitHub for AI models, the place developers discover them, compare them, customize them, and decide how to deploy them. Nvidia built its dominant position from the bottom up: GPUs provided the compute, CUDA created the programming environment around that compute, and networking plus DGX systems expanded that into complete AI infrastructure. Hugging Face moves Nvidia one step closer to the developer, sitting at the exact decision point of which model to use and where to run it.
A real economic logic sits underneath the deal. The largest frontier AI companies count among Nvidia’s biggest customers, and those same companies carry the strongest incentive to build alternative accelerators and custom silicon. Open AI creates a fundamentally different market structure instead: millions of developers, thousands of organizations, millions of models, and an enormous variety of workloads. That fragmentation suits a broadly programmable accelerated-computing platform well. Nvidia doesn’t need to win the model war outright. It benefits simply if nobody else does.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang went unusually far in promising Hugging Face stays open. Developers keep the freedom to choose their own models, frameworks, clouds, inference providers, and computing platforms, and Nvidia explicitly stated its own compute will not become a requirement for building on or deploying through the platform. Justin Boitano, Nvidia’s enterprise computing general manager, framed the strategy directly: Growing Hugging Face’s user base depends on keeping developers free to choose their own hardware, clouds, and stack, even as Nvidia benefits from the training and inference that happens to run on Nvidia hardware anyway.
“Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” Huang posted on X. “They allow every developer, startup, university, industry and country to build with, customize and benefit from AI.”
That commitment isn’t simple goodwill. It’s fundamental to the acquisition’s actual value. Hugging Face became important precisely because it functions as a broadly accessible meeting place for the entire AI community, and turning it into an Nvidia-only channel would undermine the exact ecosystem Nvidia just paid nearly $13 billion to acquire. Nvidia doesn’t need that kind of exclusivity. It only needs its own path through the platform to run exceptionally well, letting a developer discover a model on Hugging Face, evaluate it, optimize it for Nvidia hardware, and deploy it through Nvidia’s own growing software stack, all without technically closing off any other path. The real competitive question isn’t whether Hugging Face keeps supporting AMD, Intel, and other accelerators; it’s whether Nvidia’s own path becomes so frictionless that neutrality stops mattering in practice.
The acquisition extends well past hyperscale cloud, too. Huang specifically described open models reaching factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms, and Main Street businesses, running across cloud GPUs, enterprise servers, AI workstations, local AI appliances, PCs, edge systems, and robots. Deploying a model increasingly means an RTX workstation, a DGX-class appliance, an edge server, or an autonomous machine, connecting Hugging Face directly to Nvidia’s push into local AI, robotics, and physical AI.
Hugging Face itself carries a genuinely French origin story. Three Frenchmen—Clement Delangue, Julien Chaumond, and Thomas Wolf—founded the company in New York back in 2011, originally building a conversational AI interface aimed at teenagers, a rough forerunner of ChatGPT. The platform pivoted toward businesses and professionals, then took off sharply once ChatGPT itself launched and generative-AI use exploded. Hugging Face turned down multiple stake purchases and takeover offers before choosing Nvidia, citing its stated commitment to the open ecosystem. French Economy Minister Roland Lescure called the deal a “wake-up call” for Europe’s own capital markets, warning that start-ups without enough local capital will keep finding it elsewhere.
Nvidia’s own free cash flow, expected to be near $200 billion for fiscal year 2027, makes the $13 billion price tag look small by comparison. The harder question isn’t affordability. It’s whether Nvidia can keep Hugging Face genuinely neutral, making its own path through the platform good enough at the same time that neutrality stops being the thing developers actually choose.
The neutrality pledge is the deal’s real load-bearing wall, not a talking point. Nvidia doesn’t need every model built on its hardware; it needs the best path through Hugging Face to run on Nvidia silicon specifically. Watch whether that “exceptionally good” Nvidia path stays a genuine choice among equals or quietly becomes the default nobody bothers avoiding.
Inflection point. Nvidia already owns the compute layer through GPUs and the programming layer through CUDA. Hugging Face adds the discovery layer, the actual point where a developer picks which model to use. Owning that decision point, keeping it technically open at the same time, marks a genuine inflection point in how AI infrastructure competition works: The fight stops being purely about who ships the fastest chip and becomes about who sits closest to the moment a developer decides where their workload runs.

title: Nvidia купує Hugging Face за $12,93 млрд
lead: Nvidia підтвердила придбання платформи відкритих AI-моделей Hugging Face за $12,93 млрд; угода має закритися в першій половині 2027 року за умови регуляторного схвалення.
full: Nvidia офіційно оголосила про угоду в четвер, після чого її акції зросли приблизно на 2%. Hugging Face — платформа, яку описують як «GitHub для AI»: на ній розміщено понад 3 млн моделей, 500 тис. датасетів і 1 млн застосунків, а користуються нею понад 18 млн розробників і дослідників та понад 200 тис. компаній, які знаходять, оцінюють, кастомізують і розгортають AI-моделі. Платформу заснували 2011 року в Нью-Йорку троє французьких інженерів — Клеман Деланг, Жульєн Шомон і Тома Вольф.

CEO Nvidia Дженсен Хуанг публічно пообіцяв, що Hugging Face залишиться відкритою: розробники збережуть свободу вибору моделей, фреймворків, хмар і провайдерів інференсу, а власне залізо Nvidia не стане обов'язковою умовою для роботи на платформі. Генеральний менеджер напряму enterprise computing Джастін Бойтано пояснив, що зростання аудиторії Hugging Face прямо залежить від збереження цієї нейтральності, навіть попри те, що Nvidia все одно виграє, коли тренування й інференс відбуваються на її власному залізі. Фактично угода додає до інфраструктури Nvidia (GPU як обчислювальний шар і CUDA як програмний шар) ще й «шар відкриття» — точку, де розробник обирає, яку модель використати.

Міністр економіки Франції Ролан Лескюр назвав угоду «дзвіночком» для європейських ринків капіталу, зауваживши, що стартапам без достатнього місцевого фінансування доводиться шукати гроші деінде. Вільний грошовий потік Nvidia на 2027 фінансовий рік прогнозується на рівні близько $200 млрд, тож $13 млрд за Hugging Face — відносно невелика сума для компанії. Угода поки очікує регуляторного схвалення і має закритися в першій половині 2027 року.
means: Hugging Face — основне місце, де можна знайти відкриті моделі для інпейнту, релайту, денойзу, глибини, апскейлу та портретної ретуші, які потенційно можна інтегрувати в наші продукти (Erase, Relight AI, Noiseless AI, Supersharp AI, Mask AI). Поки Nvidia публічно обіцяє зберегти нейтральність платформи щодо заліза й хмарних провайдерів, тож умови доступу до моделей формально не міняються, але варто стежити, чи не зміняться ліцензійні умови або пріоритизація моделей, оптимізованих під Nvidia, у міру наближення закриття угоди. Акцент Nvidia на локальному й edge-розгортанні (PC, робочі станції, edge-пристрої) також може пришвидшити появу моделей, оптимізованих під on-device сценарії, що релевантно для Luminar Mobile.

Home / Latest / Latest news / I came back with over 20,000 images from my ‘relaxing’ city break – here’s how I organised and edited them so quickly!
You’re back from a fabulous holiday, now all that’s left is the daunting task of sorting through your thousands and thousands of travel photographs. To organise and sort his travel pictures, Will Cheung took the easy route and turned to Excire Foto 2027 There’s nothing like travel to get your creative juices flowing and the shutter finger working. For my recent holiday to Hong Kong, I didn’t have huge photographic ambitions, so I packed what I would consider a decent outfit because I didn’t want to get caught short, but neither did I take the kitchen sink approach.
At the heart of my kit was a couple of cameras, the Canon EOS R5 and EOS R5 Mark II , and they were supported by four zooms: a RF 14-35mm f/4 IS USM, RF 24-105mm f/4 IS USM, RF 70-200mm f/2.8L IS USM and RF 100-500mm f/4.5-7.1L IS USM.
The final lens was one I used a lot and that was a RF 28mm f/2.8 STM prime which was small, portable and reasonably fast. A Gitzo Series 1 Traveler carbon tripod and a set of Kase Armour filters rounded off my outfit. So quite a gear collection, but on days out in Hong Kong I only took out what I would use rather than what I thought I might use.
For urban walks I took the three zooms covering from 14mm to 200mm, while on the few occasions we went to parks or nature reserves, the RF 100-500mm f/4.5-7.1L IS USM was the mainstay and that was great for butterflies, dragonflies and birds.
Working through 24,000 raw images, the easy way
Over the fortnight’s holiday I took close to 24,000 raws, which is quite productive considering that photography was not the top priority and I just wanted a great break in a lovely city. On trips where I know I’m going to be busy with the camera I take my MacBook Air laptop and a portable external hard drive and at end of each day I would upload the shots into a folder with the date and location where I had been. There are two reasons for this. One, as back up in case something happens to the memory card. Two, this speeds up my workflow when I get home and with all my photos in folders ready to transfer to my storage hard drives. It sounds a tad fussy but it’s a system that works for me and putting in a little effort each night saves time back at base.
Another big time saver in my workflow is Excire Foto 2027, an AI-powered image management software that I use it to keep my 800,000 plus images organised.
I used to rely on Adobe Lightroom for this but now I cull rejects and images I’ll never use in Excire Foto 2027 first. Sifting through thousands of raw shots in Lightroom, rating and deleting as you go, is slow compared with Excire Foto 2027 where flicking through a serious number of images is a treat rather than a chore.
Large previews are refreshed almost instantly and there’s no waiting for images to sharpen up and once the shoot is thinned down, it’s imported into Lightroom for editing.
Using Excire Foto 2027 with existing images is straightforward too and once images are rated, the details can be transferred to current Lightroom catalogues. I started working with its predecessor, Excire Foto 2025, a couple of years ago but when Excire Foto 2027 was unveiled earlier this year all the improvements made upgrading to the latest version the obvious thing to do.
All the search features are available but now there is AI Text Recognition, Map view which takes GPS details from files and shows where photos were taken and a Timeline function where you view images taken at a particular time, even down to a specific day. There’s also an improved interface with a new-look search bar and Survey view where you can select a number of images which are displayed against a plain black background and as images are eliminated the remaining get bigger. It makes the funnelling down the selections a pleasure.
Automatic keywording is an incredibly useful skill of Excire Foto 2027 and another potential time saver and if, like me, you lack commitment in the keywording department, having a software do it for you is a good thing. Find by Text Prompt is a powerful, effective and versatile search tool. Just type in what you are looking for, which might be a specific subject, but you can try describing a particular theme or emotion and Excire Foto 2027 will use its AI powers to find suitable images. To show its effectiveness, I knew I had taken quite a few images of Hong Kong trams on my trip, so I performed a Find by Text Prompt search for ‘Hong Kong trams’ through the entire 800,000 image database. In a few seconds Excire Foto 2027 accurately identified 3650 tram images.
If you’ve spent a lot of money and time on kit and travel, it stands to reason that looking after your images is important and any process or software that can help should be considered. Excire Foto 2027 is fast and easy to use, boasts very powerful search tools and has an impressive line-up of photographer-friendly features. If you find managing your images time-consuming and even painful, Excire Foto 2027 could be your ideal solution.
The new Excire Foto 2027 app retains all the rating, culling and search skills of Foto 2025 plus it has gained several significant features.
AI Text Recognition gives a new way of searching the image database and the software will automatically detect visible text in your images, and it does this quickly. It means if you’re looking for a place name, street, shop front or brand name, you can do it accurately and very quickly.
Another major feature is Map View. Excire Foto 2027 automatically detects GPS data – whether embedded at the time or added post-shoot – in your images and videos and places where you shot the content on an interactive map.
Click on an appropriate location and you immediately see all the images shot there. It’s a great tool for travel, street and landscape photographers.
If you need to find images taken at a particular time frame, there’s a powerful timeline tool and it’s intuitive to use too. Just zoom into the timeline graph and the date you are looking for, and you see the images instantly and then you can rate, keyword and discard your work as normal.
Excire Foto 2027’s workflow is now even more efficient with, among other features, a redesigned search bar and Survey view, where you can assess images quickly in an uncluttered interface. Watch out for a full review soon.

AI content creation platform, Picsart, has appointed Lusine Yeghiazaryan as Chief Financial Officer as the company shifts its focus from photo editing toward a video-first, AI-powered production model.
Yeghiazaryan joins from SADA Systems, where she served as CFO and oversaw the company’s expansion into new services and AI revenue segments, managed a partnership with Google Cloud and led SADA’s strategic sale to Insight Enterprises. Her career also includes management roles at Diebold Nixdorf, Deloitte and GoPro.
Picsart, which has more than 100 million monthly active users and over 2.5 billion downloads, is expanding beyond its origins as a photo-editing platform into what the company describes as a comprehensive creative technology stack.
The company reports that its users have created more than 1.1 billion AI videos and images since launch, with year-to-date AI usage up 270 per cent year-on-year based on internal data from August 2025 to August 2026.
The platform’s ecosystem now includes video-first tools, a Creative AI Agent Marketplace, CLI and MCP integration compatible with Claude and Codex, and desktop expansion via AI Playground.
As CFO, Yeghiazaryan will lead global financial strategy, with an initial focus on aligning Picsart’s financial trajectory with its video-first direction while balancing fiscal discipline with the pace of investment required for AI-led growth.
Founder and CEO of Picsart, Hovhannes Avoyan, framed the appointment as arriving at a turning point for both the company and the creative technology market.
“As AI and video transform how people create and communicate, we are focused on scaling the opportunities with the greatest potential to drive long-term growth and value,” Avoyan explained. “Lusine’s experience building and guiding high-growth technology businesses will be instrumental as we execute on that ambition.”
Yeghiazaryan pointed to the combination of Picsart’s user base, consumer engagement and market positioning as factors in her decision to join.
“Picsart has the rare combination of global scale, strong consumer affinity and significant upside across some of technology’s most dynamic markets,” Yeghiazaryan commented. “I’m excited to help shape the company’s next chapter by pairing ambitious investment in AI and video with disciplined execution and a clear focus on monetisation and value creation.”

Почати можна без облікового запису Adobe, а вхід у безкоштовний акаунт відкриває додаткові функції.

Серед сценаріїв — генерація зображень і відео через Firefly, створення PDF з файлів і таблиць, пошук у бібліотеці Creative Cloud за темою чи настроєм, адаптація креативів під розміри соцмереж і пакетна обробка фото: видалення фону та відволікаючих обʼєктів, корекція світла й тону, кадрування і ресайз наборів знімків (хедшоти, фото з подій, товарні картки).

Adobe називає це частиною стратегії виносити свої інструменти в AI-чатботи: інтеграції вже є для ChatGPT, Claude і Copilot, Gemini обіцяють незабаром. Для точного піксельного контролю користувача перенаправляють у повноцінні застосунки — Photoshop, Premiere, Firefly.
means: Adobe перетворює редагування на агентний сценарій: «видали фон і вирівняй світло на цих 30 фото» виконується без відкриття редактора. Це тисне на цінність наших Erase, Relight AI і пакетних пресетів як окремих кроків у застосунку. Для Luminar Neo варто оцінити MCP-обгортку над хмарними інструментами (GenErase, Sky AI, Enhance) — це дешевий канал дистрибуції в чатботи, який Adobe уже займає.

Presets that carry AI masks are the trick most landscape shooters overlook, and they can shave real minutes off every edit. Fall gives you a short window of color, cool air, and quieter parks, so the less time you spend clicking through the same steps in Lightroom Classic, the more frames you bring home.
Building a workflow around virtual copies and reusable masks is exactly what Terry Vander Heiden walks through, using three shots from Grand Teton National Park. Vander Heiden starts with a shortcut worth memorizing: highlight a batch of images, hold Shift to select the range, then press Command and the apostrophe key to spin up virtual copies of everything at once. That gives you a safe copy to experiment on while your original stays untouched. From there, he moves into a black-and-white conversion that leans on the clipping view rather than guesswork. Tapping the letter J lights up the highlight and shadow warnings, and holding the Option or Alt key while dragging the white and black sliders shows you precisely where detail burns out or crushes to pure black.
Once the tones are set, the color mixer becomes the real workspace for black and white. Vander Heiden pushes the reds to make the snow on the peaks separate, warms the oranges and yellows to lift the foliage, and drops the blues to darken the sky into something with punch. He then saves the whole recipe as a custom preset called "black and white landscape," which he's clear about treating as a starting point instead of a finished look. His stance on presets is refreshingly practical: you don't need to buy someone else's, you build your own to match how you like your images, then hover over other shots to preview the same settings before committing. That habit alone changes how fast you can move through a card full of similar frames.
The part that pays off most is masking. Lightroom's AI-driven landscape masks split an image into sky, mountains, vegetation, water, and natural ground automatically, and Vander Heiden bakes those masks straight into a preset so they regenerate on any new photo. Apply the preset, wait a second or two, and every mask appears fresh for that specific image rather than copied blindly from another. If Lightroom can't find something, say natural ground, it flags the mask with a small yield sign and you simply delete it. He shows both approaches: one preset that carries your actual adjustments for a run of near-identical shots, and a leaner preset that only generates the masks so you're free to edit each one on its own terms.
The bigger shift here is treating your catalog like an assembly line before you ever touch a slider. Bring a full trip's worth of landscapes in, run the mask preset across all of them, and every image is now pre-segmented and ready. This mirrors how Lightroom's masking has evolved since Adobe introduced AI-based Select Sky and Select Subject, then expanded into object detection that now recognizes distinct scene elements. Leaning on that means your local adjustments stop being one-off manual selections and become repeatable moves you can dial the same way every time. For anyone shooting the same location across a week, that consistency is what keeps a set of photos looking like they belong together, and it frees you to make creative calls on light and color instead of redrawing the same gradient over a ridgeline again and again. It fits best when your images share a structure, a horizon, a mountain line, a foreground of grass or water, which is precisely what fall landscape trips tend to produce.
Vander Heiden also covers housekeeping that keeps the panel clean, including hiding the portrait presets you'll never use through the manage presets menu and deleting user presets you no longer need, with a fair warning that deletions can't be recovered.
Watch the full walkthrough in the video above to see the clipping and color-mixer moves in action before your next fall shoot.

title: Lightroom Classic: пресети з AI-масками перегенеровують сегментацію на кожному фото
lead: Fstoppers розбирає робочий процес Terry Vander Heiden: у Lightroom Classic AI-маски ландшафту (небо, гори, рослинність, вода, земля) зберігаються в пресет і автоматично перебудовуються під кожен новий знімок.
full: Маски Lightroom, засновані на розпізнаванні сцени, можна запекти у користувацький пресет. Після застосування до нової фотографії програма за секунду-дві генерує маски саме для цього кадру, а не копіює їх із попереднього. Якщо елемент (наприклад, природний ґрунт) не знайдено, маска позначається попередженням і її просто видаляють.

Автор показує два варіанти: пресет із повним набором правок для серії схожих кадрів і «легкий» пресет, який лише створює маски, залишаючи редагування вручну. Ідея — прогнати всю поїздку через масковий пресет одразу після імпорту, щоб кожен кадр був попередньо сегментований. Також описано швидке створення віртуальних копій, перегляд кліпінгу та чорно-білу конверсію через Color Mixer.
means: У Luminar Neo Mask AI вміє те саме розпізнавання (небо, вода, рослинність, людина), але сценарій «маски як частина пресета, що перегенеровуються на кожному фото» — сильний аргумент Lightroom для пакетної роботи. Варто перевірити, чи наші Presets із локальними правками на Mask AI відпрацьовують так само автоматично на новому знімку, і показати це в комунікації.
